front_guarantees.title: The Coalition Charter
front_guarantees.description: A signature in Baghdad will not settle every dispute between the Front's parties. Ministers and workplace delegates need enforceable rules for representation, appointments and working conditions. A funded labour charter can turn their cooperation into steadier civilian production while binding the government to the social commitments on which that cooperation rests.
front_guarantees.reference: PER_utilize_workers_house (05_iran.txt), cost 7.2: industrial cooperation through labour institutions, efficiency growth +10%, health and welfare costs -5% each. Iraqi adaptation funds civilian productivity rather than stacking another efficiency-growth reward.
front_guarantees.rationale: Integrates the former labour decision into the existing coalition charter; actual accepted and maintained Front membership remains required. Replaces administrative filler with civilian output and funded social obligations.

baath_monopoly.title: Exclusive Party State
baath_monopoly.description: The party can reserve the commanding offices of the Iraqi state for its own members. Provincial organizations, ministries and military appointments would answer to a single executive chain, allowing the leadership to assemble reserves and issue orders more quickly. Political exclusion will also deprive those institutions of experienced people whose cooperation cannot simply be commanded.
baath_monopoly.reference: SOV_academy (05_russia.txt), cost 3: mobilization +5%, planning +5%, training time -10%, terrain penalty reduction +10%. IRQ_restore_faith_in_army (05_iraq.txt), cost 7.19: 25 army experience and 25 command power with actual military spending.
baath_monopoly.rationale: Replaces political-power filler with executive mobilization while preserving the expertise penalty and the Front-versus-monopoly choice. The one-time command-power grant is supplied by the focus delivery hook, not repeated here.

defence_readiness.title: Sustainable Readiness
defence_readiness.description: Readiness rests on staff work, maintained equipment and units that can assemble before a crisis has passed. A national exercise will test the schools, depots and command arrangements established throughout the military programme. Its additional personnel commitment must be funded alongside the training itself.
defence_readiness.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army (05_iraq.txt), cost 7.19: 25 army experience, 25 command power and increased military spending. SOV_academy (05_russia.txt), cost 3: a durable planning and training institution.
defence_readiness.rationale: Retains the existing experience and planning rewards and funds the former readiness decision through its owning focus. The separate one-time delivery hook grants the 90-day readiness programme.

foreign_kuwait.title: Gulf Commercial Office
foreign_kuwait.description: Basra's merchants deal with Gulf shipping, banks and trading houses whose business depends on reliable accounts and enforceable contracts. A commercial office will bring customs specialists, investment advisers and financial services together in the port city. Their work can strengthen Iraqi commerce while giving Baghdad a better understanding of its neighbours' interests.
foreign_kuwait.reference: IRQ_bring_in_tech_companies (05_iraq.txt), cost 8.6: two offices in state 557 with treasury cost 26. Iraqi 1970 adaptation provides one offices building in Basra for 3% of GDP.
foreign_kuwait.rationale: Replaces an opinion-only conference and a tax-only focus outcome with a guarded Iraqi commercial asset. State ownership, control, capacity and one-time reward receipts remain mandatory.

foreign_arab_reconciliation.title: Regional Development Bureau
foreign_arab_reconciliation.description: Competing claims to Arab leadership have too often obstructed useful economic work. A development bureau can prepare Iraqi proposals, compare financing terms and maintain the technical contacts needed to bring regional projects to negotiation. A consistent service will give Baghdad greater influence through work that other governments can judge on its merits.
foreign_arab_reconciliation.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt), cost 7: investment duration and cost -25% with domestic trade-offs. This Iraqi bureau uses a smaller duration benefit and diplomatic capacity instead of an opinion-only conference.
foreign_arab_reconciliation.rationale: Provides a domestic institution with an actual investment effect. It neither ratifies a foreign agreement nor changes another country's obligations.

bakr_treaty.title: Soviet Procurement Office
bakr_treaty.description: Soviet equipment already places practical demands on Iraqi stores, workshops and training establishments. A permanent procurement office can bring together officers, interpreters and technical specialists who understand those demands. Common specifications and better purchasing records will help the army maintain its equipment and prepare future negotiations with Moscow.
bakr_treaty.reference: IRQ_restore_faith_in_army (05_iraq.txt), cost 7.19: 25 army experience and 25 command power. Existing Iraqi 1970 procurement reward is retained at 15 army experience with bounded supply and licensed-production benefits.
bakr_treaty.rationale: Recasts the former friendship offer as Iraqi procurement capacity; preserves the existing material reward exactly once.

royal_jordan.title: Hashemite Liaison
royal_jordan.description: Relations with Jordan require officials who can turn familiar names and personal contacts into practical business. A Hashemite liaison service will prepare commercial proposals, maintain military purchasing contacts and guide investors through Iraqi procedures. Its standing will depend on competent work in Baghdad as much as access to Amman.
royal_jordan.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt), cost 7: investment duration and cost -25%. Existing Iraqi 1970 liaison capacity retains the smaller investment-cost and licensed-production benefits.
royal_jordan.rationale: Replaces a pure-opinion treaty offer with domestic liaison work while preserving current rewards and royal government guards.

royal_commerce.title: Commercial Representation
royal_commerce.description: Iraqi firms need representatives able to explain their contracts, resolve administrative questions and guide investment applications through the ministries. A commercial service can make those arrangements easier to use and strengthen the taxable business conducted through Iraqi offices. Supporting that access will require concessions in the government's wider revenue arrangements.
royal_commerce.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt), cost 7: investment duration and cost -25% with domestic trade-offs. Existing Iraqi commercial-service effects and their revenue concession are preserved.
royal_commerce.rationale: Places the existing investment and commercial-tax rewards in a domestic institution instead of a pure-opinion partnership offer.

foreign_partner_offer.title: Foreign Technical Standards
foreign_partner_offer.description: Imported machinery is useful only when Iraqi engineers can specify, inspect and maintain it. A technical standards office will collect foreign industrial specifications and turn them into guidance for our own factories. Shared testing procedures and translated manuals will help Iraqi industry absorb equipment from a wider range of suppliers.
instant: add_tech_bonus = { name = COLDWAR_IRQ_overhaul_foreign_partner_offer_CAT_industry bonus = 0.35 uses = 1 category = CAT_industry }
foreign_partner_offer.reference: IRQ_foreign_advisors (05_iraq.txt), cost 7.19: technical cooperation supports a real construction modifier. Iraqi domestic adaptation retains its existing single-use 35% industrial research bonus.
foreign_partner_offer.rationale: Retains the existing research grant exactly once and removes the implication that a focus can obtain a foreign treaty by itself.

foreign_syria.title: Syrian Transport Links
foreign_syria.description: The roads and freight routes leading toward Syria are important to Iraqi commerce despite the rivalry between the two Baathist governments. Transport engineers can survey the Iraqi approaches, standardize maintenance plans and prepare better connections to the frontier. These works will strengthen our network and provide a sound basis for any later negotiations over cross-border traffic.
instant: add_tech_bonus = { name = COLDWAR_IRQ_overhaul_foreign_syria_CAT_infrastructure bonus = 0.35 uses = 1 category = CAT_infrastructure }
foreign_syria.reference: IRQ_trade_with_syria (05_iraq.txt), cost 5: substantive commercial rewards alongside relations and influence. Iraqi domestic adaptation retains its existing infrastructure construction and single-use research rewards.
foreign_syria.rationale: Replaces a pure-opinion conference with Iraqi transport preparation; preserves the existing research grant exactly once.

agri_river_talks.title: River Basin Planning
agri_river_talks.description: Iraqi farms depend on rivers whose flow is shaped far beyond any one district. A basin planning service will bring hydrological surveys, irrigation requirements and engineering studies into a common programme. Better knowledge of seasonal shortages can guide domestic works and give our negotiators a firmer understanding of the water on which Iraqi agriculture depends.
instant: add_tech_bonus = { name = COLDWAR_IRQ_overhaul_agri_river_talks_CAT_infrastructure bonus = 0.35 uses = 1 category = CAT_infrastructure }
agri_river_talks.reference: IRQ_foreign_advisors (05_iraq.txt), cost 7.19: engineering expertise feeds an actual construction modifier. Existing Iraqi 1970 infrastructure construction and single-use research rewards are preserved.
agri_river_talks.rationale: Turns the opinion-only water offer into a domestic planning institution without inventing a water treaty or duplicating its research reward.

iip_arab_offer.title: Arab Commercial Delegations
iip_arab_offer.description: Commercial delegations can connect Iraqi firms and public agencies with the markets and technical expertise of neighbouring Arab countries. Officials trained in investment procedures, procurement and contract law will help Iraqi institutions make better use of those contacts. The government's credibility will rest on proposals that can withstand scrutiny from merchants and parliamentary representatives alike.
iip_arab_offer.reference: SOV_back_to_the_west (05_russia.txt), cost 7: investment duration and cost -25%. Existing Iraqi 1970 civilian commercial programme preserves smaller investment-duration and licensed-production benefits.
iip_arab_offer.rationale: Replaces a pure-opinion partnership offer with domestic commercial representation under the existing IIP government guards.

foreign_incident_channel.title: Frontier Liaison Offices
foreign_incident_channel.description: Patrol reports often reach Baghdad through separate military and civil chains, leaving ministers to judge a frontier incident from incomplete accounts. Liaison offices can bring those reports together, maintain clear contact lists and prepare a common assessment for the general staff. Better information and practiced procedures will help commanders respond before uncertainty hardens into a crisis.
foreign_incident_channel.reference: SOV_academy (05_russia.txt), cost 3: planning +5% alongside trained mobilization and staff work. Existing native army_intel_factor supports the Iraqi liaison institution's limited intelligence benefit.
foreign_incident_channel.rationale: Replaces the opinion-only incident menu and diplomatic-cost modifier with bounded Iraqi intelligence and planning capacity.
